back_content: To move a ball along with subtle short taps using a stick or foot. Example: Jay learned how to dribble the hockey ball.
A soft dry crackling sound made by leaves or paper moving. Example: Gopi heard a rustle among dry leaves in the yard.
Took hold of something suddenly or roughly. Example: He grabbed his hockey stick eagerly.
Not knowing or realizing that something is taking place. Example: The scooter driver was unaware of the ball in his basket.
An outdoor area provided for children to play sports and games. Example: They met at the local playground every evening.
A dull, heavy sound such as that made by an object falling to the ground. Example: The ball landed on dry leaves with a thud.
A container attached to a vehicle or carried by hand. Example: The ball bounced right into the scooter's front basket.
Suddenly start laughing loudly together. Example: The children burst into laughter when the ball rode away.
Made or became tight or tighter; firm grip. Example: Jay tightened his grip around the stick handle.
A remarkable concurrence of events without apparent causal connection. Example: It was an amusing coincidence that the ball landed in the basket.
Snatched, seized, grasped. Example: He grabbed the ball before it rolled away.
Aware, conscious, mindful. Example: He was aware of the rules of the game.
Gripped, squeezed, secured. Example: He tightened his belt before running.
Loosened, slackened, relaxed. Example: He loosened his grip on the handle.
Thump, bang, clatter. Example: The heavy book fell with a thud.
Crying, weeping, sorrow. Example: Laughter filled the playground instead of sorrow.
Tap, guide, maneuver. Example: She can dribble the ball past defenders.
Silent letter 't' in rustle (/ˈrʌs.əl/). The 't' is not pronounced.
Two syllables (/ˈdrɪb.əl/). Double 'b' creates a short 'i' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈskuː.tər/). Double 'o' makes a long '/uː/' sound.
Silent letter 'w' in wrist (/rɪst/). Example: Jay tightened his wrist around the stick.
Two syllables (/ˈlɑːf.tər/). The 'gh' makes an '/f/' sound.
Was not. Example: The scooterist wasn't aware of the ball.
Could not. Example: The children couldn't catch up to the fast scooter.
They had / They would. Example: They'd never seen a ball disappear like that!
There is / There has. Example: There's a white ball lying in the garden.
Let us. Example: Let's play a game of hockey!

front_content: Gone with the wind / Gone in a flash
back_content: Disappeared very quickly without a trace. Example: The ball was gone in a flash with the scooter.
To suddenly start laughing heartily. Example: Everyone burst into laughter at the unexpected sight.

front_content: Out of sight, out of mind
back_content: If you don't see something, you forget about it. Example: Once the scooter drove away, the ball was out of sight.
At the height of activity or enthusiasm. Example: The hockey match was in full swing when the ball cleared the gate.
To surprise someone when they are not expecting it. Example: The hard hit caught the fielders off guard.
